reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical ordinary Lebesgue volume; dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal and eta:R. Assume alpha cast to R is strictly positive, alpha<=beta, V is C2, and for all x,a in E,
  alpha*||a||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a <= beta*||a||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define the actual measures and potential
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g),mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta).
The tilt has density exp(-V)/integral exp(-V) with respect to volume; prod/map/stdGaussian are the actual independent product, pushforward and standard real Hilbert Gaussian.
There exist kernels R,S:E->Measure E satisfying all the following: both are Markov kernels; R is a conditional kernel disintegrating the swapped actual joint J.map Prod.swap; and for every y in E, S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For every y in E, S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is volume-integrable, and its volume integral is strictly positive. For this y there exists a real-linear partial operator D:L2(S(y);R)->L2(S(y);E) with dense domain in scalar L2(S(y)), D closable and D.closure closed. Its graph is exactly characterized by: for every scalar L2 a and vector L2 H, (a,H) is in graph(D) iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real function q with a=q S(y)-almost everywhere and H=gradient(q) S(y)-almost everywhere.
For this same D, for every real epsilon>0 and every f in L2(S(y);R), there exists u in D.closure.domain satisfying all conclusions below simultaneously. Write u_rep and f_rep for the standard measurable representatives of the scalar quotient classes and G_rep for the actual standard vector L2 representative of G=D.closure(u). Abbreviate the displayed residual by
  r(x)=epsilon*u_rep(x)+<gradient(W_y)(x),G_rep(x)>_E-f_rep(x).
(a) For every z in D.closure.domain,
  epsilon*<u,z>_{L2(S(y);R)}+<D.closure(u),D.closure(z)>_{L2(S(y);E)}=<f,z>_{L2(S(y);R)}.
(b) u_rep and G_rep are locally integrable with respect to ordinary Lebesgue volume.
(c) For every real C1 compactly supported psi and every direction a:E, both x->psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E and x->u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable and
  integral psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E dx = - integral u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
(d) x->||r(x)||^2, using the real scalar norm, is locally volume-integrable.
(e) For every compact K in E, u_rep,G_rep,r each satisfy actual MemLp at exponent 2 with respect to volume.restrict K.
(f) For every real C2 compactly supported q, both x->u_rep(x)*Delta(q)(x) and x->r(x)*q(x) are volume-integrable and
  integral u_rep(x)*Delta(q)(x) dx = integral r(x)*q(x) dx.
(g) For every real C2 compactly supported chi, define the actual functions (v_chi denotes the statement's let-defined v)
  v_chi(x)=chi(x)*u_rep(x),
  G_chi(x)=chi(x) scalar-multiplied by G_rep(x)+u_rep(x) scalar-multiplied by gradient(chi)(x),
  F_chi(x)=chi(x)*r(x)+2*<gradient(chi)(x),G_rep(x)>_E+u_rep(x)*Delta(chi)(x).
Then v_chi,G_chi,F_chi each satisfy actual global MemLp 2 volume, and each has its topological support contained in tsupport(chi): tsupport(v_chi) subset tsupport(chi), tsupport(G_chi) subset tsupport(chi), tsupport(F_chi) subset tsupport(chi).
For every real C1 compactly supported psi and every direction a:E, both x->psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E and x->v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable, and
  integral psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E dx = - integral v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
For every real C2 compactly supported psi, both x->v_chi(x)*Delta(psi)(x) and x->F_chi(x)*psi(x) are volume-integrable, and
  integral v_chi(x)*Delta(psi)(x) dx = integral F_chi(x)*psi(x) dx.
Under this same cutoff define the actual scalar A_chi(x)=<gradient(W_y)(x),G_chi(x)>_E-F_chi(x), with exactly the minus sign before F_chi. Then v_chi,G_chi,A_chi each satisfy actual MemLp at exponent 2 with respect to S(y). There exist scalar classes vW,AW in Lp R 2 (S(y)) and a vector class GW in Lp E 2 (S(y)) such that vW=v_chi S(y)-almost everywhere, AW=A_chi S(y)-almost everywhere and GW=G_chi S(y)-almost everywhere, and simultaneously
  (vW,GW) belongs to this original D.closure.graph,
  ((alpha+1/eta)/4)*||GW||_{L2(S(y);E)}^2 <= ||AW||_{L2(S(y);R)}^2.
The scalar alpha in the coefficient is its NNReal-to-real cast and 1/eta is the real reciprocal; the quarter factor is exact. Weighted membership and inequality are conclusions about the returned actual quotient classes, not assumptions added to their existence.
One common R,S pair serves every y; one D per y is selected before all epsilon and forcing f; one actual u and its G are chosen per epsilon/f before ALL C2 compact cutoffs; each cutoff's v_chi,G_chi,F_chi,A_chi are formula-defined and its returned weighted classes are chosen afterward. All y have the stated density/operator conclusions. Conditional disintegration itself retains usual version scope, not an assertion about every possible conditional version at every y. No jointly measurable y-dependent solution or class selector is asserted.
Original Hilbert inner products and final quotient norms use S(y); all ordinary local integrability, compact restrictions, real weak-gradient/PDE integrals and localized global volume-L2 conclusions use canonical volume. MemLp means actual a.e. strong measurability and finite norm. AE class identities are under S(y), not pointwise/support equalities of quotient representatives. C2 compact cutoffs have no extra range, positivity or plateau assumption. Classical Laplacians act only on C2 tests/cutoffs; no classical derivative/Hessian of rough u or v_chi is asserted. The statement is cutoff-wise weighted closure membership and scalar coercivity; it does not remove cutoffs or assert a global coercivity/Bochner theorem, adjoint/core equality, epsilon=0/kernel/range theorem, further functional inequality, or complete kernel-composition result.

conclusion: Exists Markov R,S, R conditional for J.map Prod.swap and S y reflection pushforward for all y. For every y S y normalized tilt(-W_y), W_y C2, exp(-W_y) volume-integrable with positive partition; exists dense closable original partial gradient D, closure closed, exact smooth compact graph. For every epsilon>0/f exists same u for variational identity, volume locally integrable u/G, ordinary C1 weak-gradient both L1 products/minus equation, locally integrable ||r||^2, all compact K volume-L2 u/G/r and all C2 weak-Poisson both L1 products/equality. Every C2 compact chi gives v=chi*u,Gchi=chi*G+u*gradchi,Fchi=chi*r+2<gradchi,G>+u*Deltachi with global volumeL2,all three support inclusions and all C1/C2 ordinary weak tests with legal L1 products. With Achi=<gradW_y,Gchi>-Fchi, weighted MemLp v/Gchi/Achi 2 (S y),exists actual AE-linked weighted classes vW/AW/GW,(vW,GW) in same original D.closure.graph, and ((alpha+1/eta)/4)*||GW||^2 <= ||AW||^2.

Reflection/potential/operator facts hold every y, conditional property retains normal disintegration-version scope. Final norms/AE use S y distinct from ordinary volume weak data.
